title: MHA layerwise curvature phase transition
claim: MHA models can exhibit layerwise curvature phase transitions — topology changes from saddle (negative curvature) in early layers to valley (positive curvature) in later layers. GQA models show uniform valley throughout due to architectural confinement.
interpretation: In MHA models, the optimizer must LEARN confinement through training. This appears to progress with depth: shallow layers retain saddle geometry (no held dominant direction), deeper layers develop valley structure (confined). GQA models skip this — confinement is architectural. Same functional outcome, different mechanism.
caveats: Observed in one MHA model (GPT-2 medium). Pythia-410M shows uniform saddle (no transition). The transition may depend on training recipe, not just architecture.
Only 5 layers probed for other models vs 24 for GPT-2. Need full-depth probes for fair comparison.
p=0.014 is significant but not overwhelming with 24 data points.
